title: JavaScript ES6 Features: A Comprehensive Guide
description: The ES6 features that changed how JavaScript is written: let and const, arrow functions, destructuring, template literals, promises and modules.

blocks.v: JavaScript ES6 (ECMAScript 2015) introduced powerful features that enhance code readability, maintainability, and efficiency. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced developer, understanding these features will significantly improve your JavaScript skills.

ES6, released as ECMAScript 2015, is the version that reshaped how JavaScript is written day to day. Everything below is supported in every current browser and in Node, so none of it needs a build step or a polyfill any more. The features are ordered roughly by how often they come up in real code rather than by how advanced they are.
Arrow functions simplify syntax and make code more concise. Unlike traditional functions, they inherit the this value from their lexical scope.

const add = (a, b) => a + b;
console.log(add(5, 10)); // Output: 15

v: Useful for callbacks and array methods

blocks.v: Template literals simplify string concatenation using backticks () and allow embedded expressions with ${}`.

const name = "Bilal";
console.log(`Hello, ${name}!`); // Output: Hello, Bilal!
Destructuring allows extracting values from arrays or objects in a cleaner way.
The spread operator (...) allows expanding elements of an array or object.
Rest parameters allow functions to accept an indefinite number of arguments as an array.

const sum = (...numbers) => numbers.reduce((acc, curr) => acc + curr, 0);
console.log(sum(1, 2, 3, 4)); // Output: 10
Async/Await simplifies asynchronous operations, making them more readable and maintainable.
Maps store key-value pairs and maintain insertion order.

const set = new Set([1, 2, 3, 3]);
console.log(set); // Output: Set { 1, 2, 3 }
Default parameters assign a default value if no argument is passed.

const greet = (name = "Guest") => console.log(`Hello, ${name}!`);
greet(); // Output: Hello, Guest!
ES6 introduced modules to split code into reusable components.
The map() method creates a new array by applying a function to each element.
The filter() method returns an array with elements that meet a condition.
The reduce() method executes a function on each array element and returns a single value.
1. What is the difference between var , let , and const in ES6?

v: var has function scope, while let and const have block scope.
const cannot be reassigned after declaration.

blocks.v: 2. How does the spread operator differ from the rest parameter?

v: The spread operator expands an array/object, while the rest parameter collects multiple arguments into an array.

blocks.v: 3. Why should I use arrow functions?

v: Arrow functions provide a concise syntax and do not bind this , making them ideal for callbacks.
ES6 modules allow code splitting using import and export , making code more modular and reusable.

blocks.v: 5. How does async/await improve asynchronous programming?

v: It makes asynchronous code look synchronous, improving readability and maintainability.
